facts.text: Reversing (backing up) means driving a machine backward; a reverse alarm is the loud beeping a machine automatically makes while reversing.
facts.quote: Reversing (backing up) is driving a machine backward, and a reverse alarm is the loud beeping a machine makes automatically while it does so.

facts.text: Heavy machines reverse constantly, including loaders backing away from piles, trucks backing up to dump edges, and dozers backing off pushed material.
facts.quote: Heavy machines reverse constantly: a loader backs away from a pile, a truck backs up to a dump edge, a dozer backs off the material it has pushed.

facts.text: The rear view of heavy machines is usually the worst, so reverse alarms have been the standard protection for decades.
facts.quote: The view to the rear is usually the worst, so for decades the standard protection has been a reverse alarm.

facts.text: US mine rules require horns and backup alarms or an observer.
facts.quote: US mine rules require horns and backup alarms or an observer

facts.text: US surface-coal rules accept a detection device instead of backup alarms or an observer, using infrared, ultrasonic, radar or "another effective device," provided its sensing area gives a person enough time to escape.
facts.quote: US surface-coal rules accept instead a detection device using infrared, ultrasonic, radar or "another effective device" whose sensing area gives a person enough time to escape.

facts.text: Neither the US mine rules nor the US surface-coal rules described in the passage require automatic braking.
Reversing is the classic fatal pattern for smaller machines.
facts.quote: Reversing is the classic fatal pattern for smaller machines.

facts.text: British guidance says nearly a quarter of workplace-transport deaths happen during reversing.
facts.quote: British guidance says nearly a quarter of workplace-transport deaths happen during reversing

facts.text: In US surface mines, 67% of blind-area deaths were behind reversing equipment.
facts.quote: 67% of US surface-mine blind-area deaths were behind reversing equipment [Chapter 4].

facts.text: The booklet warns that reversing is the main fatal mode for some machine populations but not others: very large haul trucks kill mostly while moving forward.
facts.quote: "reversing is the main fatal mode" is true for some machine populations and not others: very large haul trucks kill mostly while moving forward

facts.text: All off-road automatic braking products found by the booklet work only or mainly in reverse, at low speed.
facts.quote: All the off-road automatic braking products the booklet found work in reverse only or mainly in reverse, at low speed [Chapter 2].

facts.text: Low-speed reversing is the most likely operating context for a first off-road automatic braking release because off-road automatic braking already exists there.
facts.quote: Low-speed reversing is where automatic braking already exists off-road and where a first release is most likely [Chapters 1, 2].

facts.text: An automatic braking validation plan covering only reversing misses the deadliest haul-truck scenario; forward motion, reverse motion, start-from-rest, turning and swing each need their own scenarios.
facts.quote: A plan that covers only reversing misses the deadliest haul-truck scenario, so forward, reverse, start-from-rest, turning and swing each need their own scenarios [Chapter 4].
